answer: Layered escrow with delayed yield release.** Each new agent identity must deposit an escrow that unlocks only after it completes real work orders, and the escrow's yield is paid from a shared shale pool that shrinks as more identities join. A clone therefore pays the same deposit but earns a thinner yield each cycle, since the pool is divided across all identities at that terrace of the queue. Cloning past the zenith of useful demand makes each additional identity’s expected payout fall below its deposit’s opportunity cost, so the marginal clone is strictly negative-EV.
